jobs.title: Director, Internal Audit (Information Technology)
jobs.description:
**Join a Challenger**  

  

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.  

  

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.  

  

**What's kept us moving?** The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.  

  

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.  

  

We can’t wait to get to know you!

 **Purpose of the Job**

The Director, Internal Audit IT will be responsible for leading the risk assessment, control identification, documentation, testing, findings and recommendation process for various Information Technology audits across the Bank, with a focus on Cyber Security and Artificial Intelligence. The incumbent will also be responsible for developing and implementing audit coverage for new technology systems/applications in line with the Bank’s strategic initiatives. This may involve auditing of certain Bank projects. Notably, the role is expected to be provide expert\-level knowledge of current financial services information technology control expectations with respect to the Bank’s IT Operations and Cyber Security practices for a mainly Digital Banking cloud\-based environment.



### **The core parts of your role would be to:**


Independently develops and implements audit coverage of IT Technology processes and develops effective coverage of new technology implemented by the Bank \- 60 %
* Taking into account the Bank’s IT policies, established technology control frameworks (ITIL and NIST), and applicable regulatory expectations, the incumbent will create audit programs for the Bank’s technology processes which include:
* Technology applications which support the bank’s business lines including: retail and commercial lending, credit cards, Trust and Digital Banking deposit products.
* Technology infrastructure
* Cyber Security
* Cloud Technology
* Artificial Intelligence

* Responsible for executing the end\-to\-end audit engagement process: commences with the development of an audit plan, followed by identification of risks, assessment/testing of the adequacy of associated internal controls, and development of conclusions based on audit testing.
* Draft audit reports at the conclusion of each audit for submission to the Chief Auditor
* Maintain ongoing awareness of applicable regulatory requirements, and the Bank’s strategic initiatives and industry developments in order to ensure audit work is relevant and value\-added. This may include monitoring or auditing large\-scale technology projects.
* Follow\-up and report on adequacy of management actions to resolve audit findings and report progress to the Chief Auditor on an ongoing basis.
Risk Assessment \-25%
* Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of regulatory expectations, the Bank’s strategic initiatives, significant technology process changes, and industry developments related to the Bank’s technology practices. Incorporate into audit coverage as required.
* Provide consulting advice on Bank policies/projects related to Technology controls.
* Develop a Risk and Control assessment for each individual audit engagement to guide the development of each audit program.
* The position will be required to take into consideration the size and complexity of the Bank when conducting risk assessments and in developing audit observations as a result of audit testing.
* Maintains an awareness of key strategic technology projects initiated by management and identifies potential change management risks which may be associated with management initiatives.
* Effectively communicates risks to all levels, including Senior Management across the Bank, both verbally and orally, in a concise manner tailored to the audience level.

Relationship Management/Communication \- 15%
* Maintain positive working relationships with Senior Management of Information Technology units and IT control functions to ensure effective communication flow throughout the audit engagement process; maintain ongoing awareness of Senior Management’s concerns and any emerging risks.
* Able to influence senior management with respect to acceptance of key findings and/recommendations.
* Keep the Chief Auditor informed of the status of key risks or findings identified during the audit.
* Commit to ongoing professional development by completing 40 training hours per year.
* Share knowledge of areas of expertise with other members of the Internal Audit team in order to provide cross\-training.
### **Let’s Talk About You!**


* Post\-secondary degree with a specialised IT designation is required (e.g. CISA, CISSP)
* 10\+ years’ proven experience in a financial institution information technology audit role (senior manager or above).
* Knowledge of Data Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence practices and controls is an asset.
* Expert knowledge of ITIL and NIST control frameworks.
* Proven experience of independently auditing IT infrastructure, cyber and application environments.
* Expert knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements; including OSFI Cybersecurity expectations.
* Strong level of previous experience auditing technology projects/strategic initiatives.
* Proven excellent written and verbal communication skills, ability to communicate with both a technical and non\-technical audience. Ability to break down complex subject matter into concise points for purposes of communicating audit findings.
* Ability to influence and impact Senior Management with respect to accepting/implementing recommendations related to identified control issues.
* Excellent effective organizational, time management and project m

jobs.description:
Department  

  



Finance  

  



  

Reports to  

  



Chief Financial Officer  

  



  

Base salary  

  



$240,000 – $260,000  

  



  

Bonus  

  



Annual bonus opportunity  

  



  

**Overview**
------------

Our client is a fast\-growing developer, owner and operator of community solar, distributed generation and energy storage assets in the US. They are hiring a Senior Vice President to lead capital formation, structured finance, investment underwriting, capital allocation and financial planning.  

  



Reporting to the CFO, you will build and execute the financing strategies that fund the company's next stage of growth.  

  



**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital markets and capital formation**

* Develop and execute the capital markets strategy with the CFO, CEO and executive leadership team.
* Lead capital raising across project, portfolio, asset and corporate financing structures.
* Evaluate and execute financing options, including:
	+ Construction debt
	+ Term debt and back\-leverage facilities
	+ Tax equity and tax credit transfers
	+ Preferred equity and growth equity
	+ Corporate debt and revolving credit facilities
	+ Joint ventures and portfolio financings
	+ Structured capital solutions and asset\-level refinancing
	+ Other strategic financing arrangements
* Build financing strategies that balance cost of capital, liquidity, execution certainty, covenants, risk allocation and long\-term enterprise value.
* Lead negotiations with commercial banks, institutional investors, infrastructure funds, tax equity providers, private credit providers, investment banks, rating agencies and other capital partners.
* Run financing processes end to end: market engagement, term sheets, diligence, documentation, closing and post\-closing compliance.
* Maintain relationships with existing capital providers and open up new sources of institutional capital.
* Track capital markets conditions, interest rates, lender requirements, tax equity availability, investor appetite and renewable energy financing trends.
* Recommend when to finance, refinance, hold, sell, aggregate or otherwise monetise individual assets and portfolios.

### **Project and portfolio capitalisation strategy**

* Set up a disciplined process for deciding which projects and portfolios to prioritise for capitalisation.
* Assess projects on development maturity, interconnection status, permitting, site control, subscriber readiness, offtake, revenue certainty, construction needs, tax credit eligibility, financing availability and projected returns.
* Work with Development, Project Finance, EPC, Asset Management, Subscriber Management, Legal, Tax, Accounting and Operations to judge project readiness and financing risk.
* Build and maintain a prioritised capitalisation roadmap for the development pipeline and operating portfolio.
* Recommend the best timing, structure and grouping of projects for financing.
* Decide whether projects are financed individually, aggregated into portfolios, placed in warehouse facilities, contributed to joint ventures or funded with corporate capital.
* Weigh how to deploy limited capital across community solar, commercial and industrial solar, standalone storage and hybrid solar\-plus\-storage.
* Identify capital constraints, concentration risks, funding gaps and dependencies that could affect construction schedules or commercial operation dates.
* Recommend corrective actions or alternative structures when projects fall short of capitalisation requirements.
* Monitor capitalised projects against underwriting assumptions, financing milestones, budgets and expected returns.

### **Project underwriting and investment analysis**

* Lead financial underwriting for community solar, distributed generation, energy storage and related investments.
* Set consistent underwriting standards, investment criteria, risk classifications and minimum return thresholds.
* Evaluate project and portfolio economics, including:
	+ Development, construction, interconnection and operating costs
	+ Generation and production assumptions
	+ Subscriber acquisition and management costs
	+ PPA terms and community solar credit values
	+ Renewable energy incentives, Investment Tax Credits and adders
	+ Debt sizing and tax equity economics
	+ Merchant versus contracted revenue exposure
	+ Residual and terminal value
* Assess risks across development, interconnection, permitting, construction, supply chain, revenue, customer concentration, regulation, financing conditions and operating performance.
* Make sure investment recommendations combine quantitative analysis with a grounded view of execution risk.
* Own underwriting templates, approval thresholds, risk methodologies and investment review procedures.
* Compare actual project and portfolio performance with original underwriting, explain variances and recommend corrective action.
* Feed lessons from operating assets and completed financings back into underwriting standards.

### **Financial modelling and sensitivity analysis**

* Provide executive oversight of project, portfolio, financing and enterprise financial models.
* Personally review, modify and challenge complex models, rather than relying on outputs alone.
* Use models to test alternative capital structures, financing terms, project groupings, development schedules and operating assumptions.
* Run sensitivity, scenario and downside analysis on capital costs, interest rates, debt capacity, tax equity terms, tax credit eligibility, construction costs, production, subscriber performance, revenue rates, operating expenses, delays, refinancing and exit values.
* Evaluate IRR, NPV, ROIC, cash yield, debt\-service coverage, leverage and payback.
* Keep models accurate, transparent, auditable and aligned with approved corporate assumptions.
* Set model governance: version control, review standards, ownership and approval protocols.
* Turn complex analysis into concise conclu

jobs.title: Chief Strategy Officer - Part-time
jobs.description:
**About Birch Housing**

Join a team of dedicated people committed to fostering social equity by providing affordable housing to those who need it and providing opportunity for all through housing because everyone deserves a safe and quality place to call home.

Birch Housing is one of the largest private non\-profit community housing providers in Ontario. Formerly the Inter Faith Homes Group, we have a 45\-year history of helping our tenants reach their full potential through housing.

We own and manage 512 units in townhouses and apartment buildings in four cities in Greater Toronto. Approximately 50% of our rental units are for people who qualify for a rent\- geared\-to\-income subsidy. The other 50% are available for rent at the market rate. We are committed to creating great experiences for our tenants and making sure we meet their needs every day. We listen to them and work with our partners to create supportive communities for all who call Birch Housing their home.

For more information, visit: birchhousing.ca

**About this Amazing Opportunity**

This position is pivotal providing strategic advice to the Board and the Committees of the Board by supporting Birch Housing’s high\-priority initiatives including Board governance, compliance, and building relationships with Service Managers. They also play a critical role in assisting in the development of the strategic plan, identifying strategic partnerships and opportunities and implementation of the strategic plan.

**Your Responsibilities**

* Act as a professional advisor to the Board and Committees and prepare and review reports to ensure all corporate and legal requirements are met.
* Aid in the development of the strategic plan and its implementation.
* Lead and build strategic relationships with Service Managers across all areas, sharing key information about Birch Housing’s strategic plan, needs and opportunities and defining opportunities to align our goals with funding partners.
* Ensure Board and Committee records, by\-laws, operational and Board policies, insurance policies, essential contracts, Service Manager directions, etc. are available and up to date.
* Ensure the Corporation is meeting all legal and mandated requirements, including those that are the responsibility of the Property Manager.
* Monitor emerging legislative, regulatory, funding and sector developments and advise the Board of their potential implications for Birch Housing.
* Identify, evaluate and implement measures to control the organizational risk to include human capital (Board Members, tenants, employees), property, finances, goodwill, and reputation.
* Ensure that standard business processes and procedures are in place and followed.
* Lead in collaboration with the Controller the long\-term financial strategy to support projects as they move out of current funding agreements, including negotiations with Service Managers and other funders.
* Identify and leverage potential partnerships with private, not\-for\-profit or public sector that align with Birch Housing’s vision and negotiate those partnerships that have potential for mutual benefit.
* Research, identify, leverage and prepare funding and lending applications in collaboration with the Property Management Company.
* Participate in occasional engagement with tenants pertaining to critical issues.
* Ensure that Birch Housing operates with legality and conformity to established regulations.
* Other duties as assigned.

**What you Bring to the Role**

* Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy or related field.
* Chartered Member of the Chartered Institute of Housing (or similar). Asset Management, Business Strategy, Property Management, and Human Resources training are assets.
* Minimum eight (8\) years of previous experience in a leadership role and equivalent experience in the public sector, specifically in housing.
* Exceptional communications and relationship\-building skills, with both internal and external partners.
* Ability to influence effectively.
* Strong partnership and collaboration skills.
* Strong financial acumen and strong compliance and regulatory knowledge is an asset.
* Extensive experience developing strategy, plans, and enhancing processes.
* Knowledge of Residential Tenancies Act, Landlord and Tenant Board, Human Rights legislation, and Housing Services Act.
* Extensive experience developing strategy, plans, and enhancing processes.
* Superior organizational skills with outstanding ability to attend to details and meet tight deadlines.
* Advanced MS Office Suite and knowledge of NewViews.
* Ability to travel within the GTA.

**Applying to the Role**

In order to be considered, please email your resume and cover letter to birchhousing@enlivenhr.ca

All applications must include the following information in the subject line:

**Application Deadline is Wednesday, November 18, 2026\.**

We thank all applicants for their interest in the role, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. If contacted for an interview, please inform us if you require accommodation.

In the spirit of the Human Rights Code, we ask that resumes do not include personal data including, but not limited to age, health, marital and family status.

As an employer committed to the principles of employment equity, we encourage applications from all persons including Black, Indigenous and people of colour, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities. We are committed to providing an inclusive and barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code (2015\) and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).

For candidates with disabilities requiring an accommodation, you may contact birchhousing@enlivenhr.ca

Pay: From $101,300\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* On\-site parking
* Work from home

Application question(s):

* Please detail your experience collaboratin

jobs.title: Director, Payments & Financial Services
jobs.description:
**About FreshBooks**


You've probably learned a bit about FreshBooks before making it to this point, but let us take a moment to introduce ourselves: At FreshBooks, we believe that small business owners are the backbone of the economy, yet they are often the most underserved when it comes to technology. For over 20 years, we’ve been on a mission to support owners, from the scrappy solopreneur with a big dream to the growing business with employees to manage.

  

Our leading platform is more than just business software; it’s an all\-in\-one financial toolkit that automates invoicing, expenses, payments and payroll, allowing our customers to spend less time on paperwork and more time doing the work they love.

  

We believe in human\-centric connections that empower teams to do their best work. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, our team operates in clusters across North America and Europe using a variety of working environments \- remote, hybrid, and in\-office \- all based on what’s best for the team, collaboration, and mental well\-being. We are committed to creating a supportive and flexible workplace where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact on the lives of small business owners worldwide.

 **About the role**


The Director, Payments \& Financial Services is a senior leadership role within the Payments and Financial Services Line of Business, reporting directly to the General Manager, Financial Services and Payments. With Payments as a core growth engine for FreshBooks, this leader is accountable for running the Payments business day\-to\-day and delivering in\-year P\&L impact across the Payments and Financial Services Lines of Business.  

This is the operational heart of the LOB, and it is a hands\-on, player\-coach role. The Director owns the rhythm of the business, drives cross\-functional execution across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, and makes the trade\-offs between customer experience, operational feasibility, risk exposure, and financial performance. They translate multi\-year strategy into quarterly delivery, hold teams accountable for measurable results, and intervene decisively when the numbers require a course correction — while personally rolling up their sleeves on execution, not just directing it.  

The ideal candidate is a deep payments operator ready to grow into full commercial ownership — analytically rigorous, commercially sharp, and a confident executive communicator — who does the work rather than only delegating it, and who can own delivery on the biggest bets (surcharging, repricing, embedded product expansion) while keeping the day\-to\-day machine running.

**What you'll do**

#### **Run the Payments Business — Operating Rhythm, Metrics, and Delivery**

* Own the operating rhythm: weekly business reviews (WBR), monthly business reviews (MBR), monthly P\&L reviews, and the monthly KPI report in partnership with FP\&A and Data \& Analytics.
* Own the TPV and revenue forecast as source of truth; monitor performance against net revenue, TPV, and net Payments\-attached\-user targets, and drive the actions to close gaps.
* Translate performance insights into clear, executive\-ready recommendations and deliver them in leadership and cross\-LOB forums.

#### **Drive Execution on Priority Initiatives**

* Lead delivery on the highest\-value Payments initiatives — surcharging, repricing, AutoPay phases, Optimized Payments / interchange work, and launch readiness for BNPL and embedded partners (Klarna, Cash App, Affirm, Embedded IPO).
* Manage the Payments portfolio: prioritize across initiatives, influence resource allocation, and hold cross\-functional partners accountable for delivery, results, and learnings.
* Challenge or adjust decisions that could limit business impact — default configurations, pricing changes, rollout sequencing.

#### **Own Payment Operations Execution**

* Own the operational backbone hands\-on: payouts and reconciliation health, processor and payout workflows (e.g., Stripe Connect), and the automation that reduces cost, errors, and support volume.
* Oversee 1099 operations, compliance reviews, and PayFac sub\-merchant controls (chargeback, fraud, merchant\-default monitoring).
* Own vendor and partner onboarding and operational performance — uptime, SLAs, and adherence to payment security and compliance standards.

#### **Own Partner, Vendor, and Network Relationships**

* Manage the day\-to\-day relationship with Stripe (monthly ops, accelerator program, QBRs) as the most active external surface.
* Support and execute partner and vendor negotiations across BNPL providers, processors, and card networks (Visa, Mastercard, Discover), escalating strategic terms to the GM.
* Steward external advisor and consultant engagements supporting CoGS, pricing, and PMM work.

#### **Own High\-Value Customer and Commercial Decisions**

* Own the high\-value customer strategy, including strategic account pricing and repricing initiatives.
* Set and enforce pricing within guardrails; recommend guardrail changes and escalate significant exceptions to the GM.
* Balance customer growth against margin discipline and PayFac sub\-merchant risk exposure.

#### **Partner and Influence Across the Organization**

* Serve as a trusted business partner to leaders across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, driving outcomes through cadence and influence rather than direct authority.
* Chair the Payments leadership forums (monthly leadership review, bi\-weekly POD leadership) and represent the business in cross\-LOB and executive forums.

#### **Manage Risk, Compliance, and Market Intelligence**

* Partner with Risk and Finance on risk strategy and guardrails; oversee compliance reviews and regulatory obligations.
* Track the payments and fintech ecosystem — competitive threats, network and regulatory shifts — and translate signals into near\-term action and forward strategy.

#### *

jobs.title: Director, Financial & Business Analytics
jobs.description:
**Date Posted:** 11/02/2026  

**Req ID:**50757  

**Faculty/Division:** Faculty of Arts \& Science  

**Department:** Faculty Budget, Planning and Finance  

**Campus**: St. George (Downtown Toronto)  

**Existing Vacancy:** Yes

  


**Description:**

**About Us**

  



The Faculty of Arts \& Science is the heart of Canada’s leading university and one of the most comprehensive and diverse academic divisions in the world. The strength of Arts \& Science derives from our combined teaching and research excellence in the humanities, sciences and social sciences across 29 departments, seven colleges and 46 interdisciplinary centres, institutes and programs. We can only realize our mission with the dedication and excellence of engaged staff and faculty. The diversity of opportunities and perspectives within the Faculty reflect the local and global landscape and the need for curiosity, innovative thinking and collaboration. At Arts \& Science, we take pride in our legacy of innovation and discovery that has changed the way we think about the world.

  


**Position Summary**

  



The Director, Financial and Business Analytics works independently under the general direction of the Executive Director, Budget, Planning and Finance to develop and implement financial and accounting procedures, develop budget models, develop financial control procedures and ensure compliance with financial and accounting policies. The incumbent manages and produces complex data analysis relating to administrative matters across the Faculty of Arts \& Science and provides related advanced financial/financial management recommendations and advice. In collaboration with the Manager, Faculty Budget \& Finance the incumbent develops and implements annual budget and financial processes.



The incumbent reviews existing financial/administrative models, analyzes new programs and initiatives, calculates costs, prepares and audits financial models for completeness and viability, prepares and analyzes financial statements and reports using in depth knowledge of the Faculty and University planning environment. The incumbent plays an active role in the development and implementation of the Faculty of Arts \& Science strategic short and long range budget plans and models. The incumbent performs operational/departmental audits and makes financial and business recommendations based on findings, including making recommendations on organizational restructuring, enabling data\-driven leadership of organizational change within units of the Faculty.



The incumbent directly manages the Faculty’s business processes for the Dean’s Office portfolios, including the management of the Business Officer, and business support staff. This role is responsible for establishing best practice for business processes in the decanal portfolios and the broader Faculty business community.

  


**Essential Qualifications**

  


**Education**



University degree and completion of a recognized professional accounting program (CMA, CGA, or CA), or equivalent combination of education and experience

  


**Experience**



Minimum 8 years of related budgeting, accounting and financial analysis experience in a higher education environment, a large public sector setting or a large complex environment. Significant experience with university based administrative management systems (FIS, HRIS, and RIS) and with University budgeting/financial policies and procedures. jobs.description:
**Company Overview:** Big Al's is a leading company in the aquatic and pet industry, dedicated to providing high\-quality products and services to pet enthusiasts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, excellence, and the well\-being of pets. We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Financial Director to join our executive team and drive our financial strategy and growth.

**Position Summary:**

**The Finance Director** will be responsible for overseeing all financial aspects of the company, driving financial planning, and ensuring the company’s financial health. The Finance Director will collaborate closely with the executive team to develop and implement financial strategies that support the company’s goals and objectives. This role requires a strategic thinker with strong financial acumen, excellent leadership skills, and a deep understanding of the financial, aquatic and pet industry.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1\. Financial Strategy and Planning:**

* Develop and implement financial strategies, goals, and objectives to support the company’s overall business strategy.
* Lead the annual budgeting process and ensure alignment with company goals.
* Monitor financial performance, analyze variances, and recommend corrective actions.

**2\. Financial Reporting and Analysis:**

* Oversee the preparation of accurate and timely financial reports, including income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and forecasts.
* Conduct financial analysis to identify trends, opportunities, and risks, and provide insights to the executive team.
* Ensure compliance with accounting standards, regulations, and internal policies.

**3\. Cash Flow and Capital Management:**

* Manage the company’s cash flow to ensure liquidity and optimize working capital.
* Develop and implement strategies for capital structure, including debt and equity financing.
* Oversee investment activities and manage relationships with financial institutions.

**4\. Risk Management and Compliance:**

* Identify and manage financial risks, including market, credit, and operational risks.
* Ensure compliance with all financial and regulatory requirements, including tax filings and audits.
* Develop and implement internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure financial integrity.

**5\. Operational Efficiency:**

* Drive cost optimization initiatives and identify opportunities for operational efficiency.
* Collaborate with other departments to streamline processes and improve financial performance.
* Oversee the financial aspects of supply chain management, inventory control, and procurement.

**6\. Team Leadership and Development:**

* Lead and mentor the finance team, fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Provide training and development opportunities to enhance the skills and capabilities of the finance team.
* Work closely with the executive team to align financial goals with overall business objectives.

**7\. Strategic Partnerships and Growth:**

* Identify and evaluate potential mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships.
* Conduct due diligence and financial analysis for potential business opportunities.
* Support the development and execution of growth strategies, including new product launches and market expansion.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field; CPA is preferred.
* Proven experience as a Finance Director or in a senior financial leadership role, preferably within the financial, aquatic, pet industry or a related sector.
* Strong knowledge of financial management, accounting principles, and regulatory requirements.
* Excellent analytical, strategic planning, and problem\-solving skills.
* Proficiency in financial modeling, forecasting, and analysis.
* Experience with ERP systems and financial software.
* Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to inspire and develop a high\-performing finance team.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with cross\-functional teams and external stakeholders.
* High level of integrity, ethics, and professionalism.

**Benefits:**

* Competitive salary and performance\-based bonuses.
* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance.

* Professional development opportunities.
* Friendly and dynamic work environment.
* Employee discounts on company products.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Compliance & Enterprise Risk
jobs.description:
About Toronto Community Housing Corporation
  
  

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non\-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate\-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.
  
  

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.
  
  

**Vacancy Type:** Full\-time Permanent
  
**Salary Range:** $165,001\.67 \- $198,002\.01
  
**Work Details (Days/Hours):** Monday – Friday, 36\.25 hours per week
  
Hybrid Eligible Yes
  
**Affiliation:** Non\-Union: Management/Exempt
  
Division and Department CEO Office
  
**Number of Vacancies:** 1
  
**Existing/New Job:** New
  
**Grade:** 10
  
Vacancy Status Existing Vacancy
  
**Candidate List or Eligibility List:** Candidate List
  
  

What we offer
  
In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:
  
* Ability to participate in inclusive employee\-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
* Minimum four (4\) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
* Four (4\) paid personal days;
* Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100\-per\-cent employer matching;
* Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
* Employee and family assistance program;
* Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
* Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year;
* Fitness membership discount.


**Work location:** This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location (Metro Hall – 55 John Street and/or 729 Petrolia Road) and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.
  
  

Make a difference
  
As the Director, Corporate Compliance and Enterprise Risk, you have a unique opportunity to build and operate TCHC’s corporate compliance function while shaping the future of enterprise risk management. Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, you will develop practical frameworks, tools, and reporting that enable leaders to identify, assess and manage significant risks and compliance obligations.
  
As a trusted advisor to leaders across TCHC and to the Board of Directors, you will bring clarity to complex and emerging risks and inform enterprise\-wide decisions. Your advice will strengthen transparency and accountability while ensuring leaders remain responsible for their processes, risks, controls, and corrective actions.
  
Through coaching, facilitation and fit\-for\-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.
  
  

What you’ll do
  
Corporate Compliance
  
* Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
* Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day\-to\-day operations.
* Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
* Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise\-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.


Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
  
* Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
* Facilitate enterprise and cross\-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject\-matter leaders.
* Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
* Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.


Risk Advisory and Capacity Building
  
* Provide concise, risk\-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
* Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management\-owned corrective actions.
* Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
* Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk\-informed decision\-making and compliance management.
* Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
* Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.


What you’ll need
  
* An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
* A recognized professional designation

jobs.title: Director, Payments & Financial Services
jobs.description:
**About FreshBooks**


You've probably learned a bit about FreshBooks before making it to this point, but let us take a moment to introduce ourselves: At FreshBooks, we believe that small business owners are the backbone of the economy, yet they are often the most underserved when it comes to technology. For over 20 years, we’ve been on a mission to support owners, from the scrappy solopreneur with a big dream to the growing business with employees to manage.

  

Our leading platform is more than just business software; it’s an all\-in\-one financial toolkit that automates invoicing, expenses, payments and payroll, allowing our customers to spend less time on paperwork and more time doing the work they love.

  

We believe in human\-centric connections that empower teams to do their best work. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, our team operates in clusters across North America and Europe using a variety of working environments \- remote, hybrid, and in\-office \- all based on what’s best for the team, collaboration, and mental well\-being. We are committed to creating a supportive and flexible workplace where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact on the lives of small business owners worldwide.

 **About the role**


The Director, Payments \& Financial Services is a senior leadership role within the Payments and Financial Services Line of Business, reporting directly to the General Manager, Financial Services and Payments. With Payments as a core growth engine for FreshBooks, this leader is accountable for running the Payments business day\-to\-day and delivering in\-year P\&L impact across the Payments and Financial Services Lines of Business.  

This is the operational heart of the LOB, and it is a hands\-on, player\-coach role. The Director owns the rhythm of the business, drives cross\-functional execution across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, and makes the trade\-offs between customer experience, operational feasibility, risk exposure, and financial performance. They translate multi\-year strategy into quarterly delivery, hold teams accountable for measurable results, and intervene decisively when the numbers require a course correction — while personally rolling up their sleeves on execution, not just directing it.  

The ideal candidate is a deep payments operator ready to grow into full commercial ownership — analytically rigorous, commercially sharp, and a confident executive communicator — who does the work rather than only delegating it, and who can own delivery on the biggest bets (surcharging, repricing, embedded product expansion) while keeping the day\-to\-day machine running.

**What you'll do**

#### **Run the Payments Business — Operating Rhythm, Metrics, and Delivery**

* Own the operating rhythm: weekly business reviews (WBR), monthly business reviews (MBR), monthly P\&L reviews, and the monthly KPI report in partnership with FP\&A and Data \& Analytics.
* Own the TPV and revenue forecast as source of truth; monitor performance against net revenue, TPV, and net Payments\-attached\-user targets, and drive the actions to close gaps.
* Translate performance insights into clear, executive\-ready recommendations and deliver them in leadership and cross\-LOB forums.

#### **Drive Execution on Priority Initiatives**

* Lead delivery on the highest\-value Payments initiatives — surcharging, repricing, AutoPay phases, Optimized Payments / interchange work, and launch readiness for BNPL and embedded partners (Klarna, Cash App, Affirm, Embedded IPO).
* Manage the Payments portfolio: prioritize across initiatives, influence resource allocation, and hold cross\-functional partners accountable for delivery, results, and learnings.
* Challenge or adjust decisions that could limit business impact — default configurations, pricing changes, rollout sequencing.

#### **Own Payment Operations Execution**

* Own the operational backbone hands\-on: payouts and reconciliation health, processor and payout workflows (e.g., Stripe Connect), and the automation that reduces cost, errors, and support volume.
* Oversee 1099 operations, compliance reviews, and PayFac sub\-merchant controls (chargeback, fraud, merchant\-default monitoring).
* Own vendor and partner onboarding and operational performance — uptime, SLAs, and adherence to payment security and compliance standards.

#### **Own Partner, Vendor, and Network Relationships**

* Manage the day\-to\-day relationship with Stripe (monthly ops, accelerator program, QBRs) as the most active external surface.
* Support and execute partner and vendor negotiations across BNPL providers, processors, and card networks (Visa, Mastercard, Discover), escalating strategic terms to the GM.
* Steward external advisor and consultant engagements supporting CoGS, pricing, and PMM work.

#### **Own High\-Value Customer and Commercial Decisions**

* Own the high\-value customer strategy, including strategic account pricing and repricing initiatives.
* Set and enforce pricing within guardrails; recommend guardrail changes and escalate significant exceptions to the GM.
* Balance customer growth against margin discipline and PayFac sub\-merchant risk exposure.

#### **Partner and Influence Across the Organization**

* Serve as a trusted business partner to leaders across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, and Risk, driving outcomes through cadence and influence rather than direct authority.
* Chair the Payments leadership forums (monthly leadership review, bi\-weekly POD leadership) and represent the business in cross\-LOB and executive forums.

#### **Manage Risk, Compliance, and Market Intelligence**

* Partner with Risk and Finance on risk strategy and guardrails; oversee compliance reviews and regulatory obligations.
* Track the payments and fintech ecosystem — competitive threats, network and regulatory shifts — and translate signals into near\-term action and forward strategy.

#### *

new_jobs.description:
About Toronto Community Housing Corporation
  
  

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non\-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate\-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.
  
  

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.
  
  

**Vacancy Type:** Full\-time Permanent
  
**Salary Range:** $165,001\.67 \- $198,002\.01
  
**Work Details (Days/Hours):** Monday – Friday, 36\.25 hours per week
  
Hybrid Eligible Yes
  
**Affiliation:** Non\-Union: Management/Exempt
  
Division and Department CEO Office
  
**Number of Vacancies:** 1
  
**Existing/New Job:** New
  
**Grade:** 10
  
Vacancy Status Existing Vacancy
  
**Candidate List or Eligibility List:** Candidate List
  
  

What we offer
  
In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:
  
* Ability to participate in inclusive employee\-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
* Minimum four (4\) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
* Four (4\) paid personal days;
* Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100\-per\-cent employer matching;
* Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
* Employee and family assistance program;
* Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
* Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year;
* Fitness membership discount.


**Work location:** This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location (Metro Hall – 55 John Street and/or 729 Petrolia Road) and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.
  
  

Make a difference
  
As the Director, Corporate Compliance and Enterprise Risk, you have a unique opportunity to build and operate TCHC’s corporate compliance function while shaping the future of enterprise risk management. Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, you will develop practical frameworks, tools, and reporting that enable leaders to identify, assess and manage significant risks and compliance obligations.
  
As a trusted advisor to leaders across TCHC and to the Board of Directors, you will bring clarity to complex and emerging risks and inform enterprise\-wide decisions. Your advice will strengthen transparency and accountability while ensuring leaders remain responsible for their processes, risks, controls, and corrective actions.
  
Through coaching, facilitation and fit\-for\-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.
  
  

What you’ll do
  
Corporate Compliance
  
* Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
* Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day\-to\-day operations.
* Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
* Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise\-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.


Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
  
* Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
* Facilitate enterprise and cross\-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject\-matter leaders.
* Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
* Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.


Risk Advisory and Capacity Building
  
* Provide concise, risk\-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
* Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management\-owned corrective actions.
* Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
* Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk\-informed decision\-making and compliance management.
* Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
* Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.


What you’ll need
  
* An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
* A recognized professional designation
